scope: Safari shipped launcher/private-framework resource metadata and controlled native UI observations; official WebKit integration research; bounded implementation of QtWebEngine regular/private profiles, new-window commands and tab overview. No original source recovery, engine migration or host-browser data export.

summary.recommended_route: A gated WPE WebKit 2.54.2 Qt6/QML integration proof, followed by a C++ browser-services adapter and reconstructed Safari-style frontend.
summary.decision_state: technically evidenced candidate, not runtime validated or selected for default shipping

limitations: Compiled resource text/frames do not establish dynamic layout or visible menu variants.
No original source or comprehensive Safari internals were recovered.
Safari UI, Apple services and Linux WebKit ports are distinct components.

new_shipped_artifact_inspection.conclusion: The inspected executable slice is a small launcher entry into a private Safari framework. Browser tab/download logic was not present in this launcher metadata.
new_shipped_artifact_inspection.confidence: High for the exact selected file's metadata; framework implementation unresolved.
limitations: Imports/exports may be incomplete for stripped or toolchain-hidden symbols.
Only the selected x86_64 slice was inspected in detail.
Expected framework filesystem paths were not ordinary files at the two probed paths; dyld-cache resolution and framework internals were not inspected.
No decompiler or dynamic tracing was used.

controlled_actions: Created a new window using Command-N.
Navigated that new window to about:blank.
Inspected View menu and opened Tab Overview.
Returned from Tab Overview, inspected application menu and About Safari.
Closed About and the created blank window; verified its window identifier was no longer present.
new_controlled_ui_observation.privacy_scope: Only synthesized, generic UI observations are retained. Existing window content automatically surfaced at initial app selection is excluded; no existing tab, history, bookmark, profile store, credential or download list was opened/exported. Profile-specific menu names are omitted.

observations.finding: New blank single-tab window exposes sidebar/profile controls, back/forward, Page Menu, Reading List, smart search field, reload, downloads, share, new tab and tab overview; a tab-bar group was not exposed until the second tab.

File menu exposes profile-specific new windows, private window, new tab, tab groups, Open File/Location, Close, Save As, Export as PDF, import/export browsing data and Print. Close Tab/Other Tabs were disabled for one tab and enabled after creating a second; group label changed to 'New Tab Group with 2 Tabs'.

Tab Overview has a Search Tabs field and two Local Tabs cards with thumbnail, title and close controls plus New Tab. Back/forward, sidebar and share are disabled in this state and restored on return as applicable.

View exposes toolbar customization, Favorites/Status bars, sidebar variants, Reader, Tab Overview, Downloads, reload, translation, zoom, text encoding and Enter Full Screen. Enabled states reflect blank-page context.

Application menu exposes extensions, settings, privacy report, per-site preferences, certificate details, history clearing and profile management. Per-site preferences and certificate details were disabled for about:blank.

new_controlled_ui_observation.screenshots: Unavailable: native getScreenshot reported Screenshot unavailable for Safari.
limitations: Accessibility may expose alternate or hidden commands; it does not prove every row is visibly displayed.
No pixel geometry, translucency, animation duration/easing, fullscreen reveal timing, real-page media behavior or download lifecycle was measured.
No runtime claim is made about private-mode isolation or Apple's network services.

route_comparison.fit: Good maintained Linux browser API and distribution package path; a native GTK browser frontend is possible.
route_comparison.constraint: WebKitWebView inherits GtkWidget, not QQuickItem. No turnkey QtQuick adapter was identified in this API. Foreign-window embedding would add focus/input/compositing work and is not the recommended default for the existing QML frontend.

route_comparison.api: WPE API2.0 plus upstream org.wpewebkit.qtwpe WPEView / WPEQtView QQuickItem
route_comparison.fit: Best structural candidate for keeping the QML browser chrome on Linux.
constraints: Not available by merely installing Debian's current libwpewebkit-2.0-dev: inspected runtime/development file lists lack qtwpe/QML plugin.
Build ENABLE_WPE_QT_API=ON and ENABLE_WPE_PLATFORM=ON; upstream option defaults to developer-mode setting.
Uses Qt6 Core/Quick/Gui, QuickPrivate and Qt6Test, plus GLib, Epoxy and WebKit. Needs an SDK matching the loaded Qt build.
Upstream implementation targets Linux EGL; comments name EGLFS and Wayland-EGL QPAs, and sets an OpenGL surface. Cutefish renderer/compositor integration is untested.
QML wrapper exposes basic navigation, title/progress and JS execution. Full profiles, downloads, policy, dialogs, permissions and fullscreen require an adapter.

network-session is construct-only. Upstream WPEQtView creates a default view without a supplied session, so proper normal/private isolation needs construction-time session injection, not a late QML flag.

Current project pins Linux PySide6 6.12.0, while Debian13 Qt development/private headers are 6.8.2. A plugin compiled against Debian Qt private APIs must not be assumed compatible with the pip-bundled Qt runtime.

route_comparison.fit: Not a Linux WebKit solution by itself.
route_comparison.constraint: Official Qt6 documentation says Linux Qt WebView uses QtWebEngine. macOS system-webview behavior does not establish Linux engine parity.

route_comparison.fit: Keep existing implementation available as a tested fallback until an alternative passes the Linux acceptance gate.
route_comparison.constraint: Do not call it Safari or WebKit engine parity.

milestones.name: Pin reconstruction target
milestones.deliverable: Versioned public UI behavior specification using Safari26.6.2 resource + controlled runtime evidence; separate user-configurable states and alternate AX menu rows.
acceptance: Add blank/local fixture scenarios for one tab, many tabs, new/private window, overview, permission/download dialogs and fullscreen reveal.
Capture pixels/timing only when supported; leave appearance/animation measurements explicitly incomplete otherwise.
milestones.status: Partial native menu/tab evidence captured; pixel/timing and additional scenarios remain.

milestones.name: WebKit Qt6 rendering gate
milestones.deliverable: Isolated Linux C++/QML proof using WPE2.54.2 with qtwpe enabled and a single matched Qt SDK/runtime, packaged separately from the default browser.
acceptance: A real Wayland app window renders a local HTML/CSS/JS fixture with active engine sandbox.
Keyboard, Greek text/IME, pointer, wheel, resize, focus and 100%/200% scale work under target Cutefish compositor.
A QML overlay renders correctly; no black surface or frame-orientation errors.
Repeated page/window open-close leaves no leaked web/network/GPU process.
Record engine version, Qt version, loaded plugin path and reproducible package hashes.
milestones.status: Research only; runtime integration gate not started.

milestones.name: Browser service adapter
milestones.deliverable: Engine-neutral page contract plus C++ WPE adapter for normal/ephemeral sessions, tabs/popups, downloads, find, permission/auth/file dialogs, TLS errors and fullscreen.
acceptance: Normal profile persists test cookies across restart; private profile writes no persistent test state and cannot read normal cookies.
A local download verifies content hash, collision behavior, cancel/error and cleanup.
Blocked popups/permissions and TLS errors are surfaced without silent security bypass.
New windows/popups retain the correct originating session and process ownership.
milestones.status: Bounded first improvements implemented/tested using existing QtWebEngine; full milestone incomplete.

milestones.name: Safari interaction reconstruction
milestones.deliverable: QML toolbar, sidebar, tab groups/overview, context-sensitive menus, address-field states and download popover derived from evidence.
acceptance: Each enabled menu item performs its documented action.
One-tab/two-tab/overview state transitions match the captured native behavior.
Replace find→address behavior with real page find; support normal/private windows and history.
Only claim visual/animation parity for scenarios with measured reference captures.
milestones.status: Bounded first improvements implemented/tested using existing QtWebEngine; full milestone incomplete.

milestones.name: Product completeness and default switch
milestones.deliverable: Session restore, bookmark/history management, permissions, accessibility, media and updates; set default browser only after tests.
acceptance: Regression fixtures pass on the shipped Linux image.
Security-update packaging for WPE/plugin is owned and reproducible.
Existing saved makOS bookmarks migrate without accessing the user's Safari data.
Apple-specific account/protocol integrations remain explicitly separate and unclaimed.

present_by_source: Download request UI/manager and cancellation cleanup

gaps.detail: QtWebEngine uses Chromium; swapping toolbar assets does not change engine behavior.
Every profile is offTheRecord with memory cache and no persistent cookies; File New Private Window is disabled.
File New Window is disabled; popup requests are redirected to a tab.
Hard limit of 12 tabs; no tab groups, tab overview, pinned tabs or persisted session restore established.
find currently focuses the address field rather than a page-find controller.
Only per-view back/forward exists; Show All History and Clear History are disabled.
No per-origin permission decision UI or saved grants.
WebEngineView.settings.fullScreenSupportEnabled=false; browser chrome fullscreen reveal not assessed.
Menu Save As and Print disabled; native Safari exposes corresponding commands and Export as PDF.
Reader, Reading List, profile UI, extensions, password integration, translation, iCloud, Handoff and Apple-specific services are not provided by this frontend.

prototype_before_changes.test_claim: Source audit only in this task; presence of test files is not a fresh execution result.

current_prototype.renderer: QtWebEngine/Chromium remains unchanged; no WebKit runtime claim.
implemented: Shared named regular profile with persisted cookies/cache under the makOS application data directory.
A separate off-the-record memory profile for each private window, released after its views unload.
Enabled New Window and New Private Window commands; fresh SuiteWindow helper wired by root.
Tab overview with search, pointer selection, close and new-tab controls; best-effort in-memory preview of visited current tabs.
Shared-profile download routing checks originating WebEngineView before prompting.
Close Tab menu is disabled with one tab, as observed in the native File menu.

verification.platform: macOS host, PySide6 Qt offscreen, local HTTP fixtures and temporary data only; not Linux compositor runtime
passed: tests/verify_browser_profiles.py: separate write/read processes prove persistent normal cookies; private isolation and clear-on-close; shared-normal-window cookies/download ownership; actual overview pointer select/close/new-tab and search.
tests/verify_web_page.py: local load, bookmarks, tabs and cleanup.
tests/verify_web_downloads.py: all download lifecycle checks, with explicit privateBrowsing=true fixture.

remaining: No visual/animation parity measurement; native AX observations are not screenshots.
No Linux/WPE runtime verification or engine switch.
12-tab limit remains; tab groups, pinned tabs, session restore and history UI remain absent.
Find still focuses address; page search not yet implemented.
Private windows use one profile each; cross-private-window sharing was not asserted to match Safari.
Normal cookies persist; session-only cookies may be removed by Chromium policy on exit.
Downloads/bookmarks intentionally persist when explicitly saved from a private window.
Permissions remain deny-only; content fullscreen, print, save-page and Apple account/services integrations remain absent.
